observations.summary: A deterministic Claude install probe wrote history.jsonl under the real user configuration root while host.claude.probe-authority still reported pass because only five selected paths were censused.

success_criteria: Any ordinary-file creation, modification, or deletion anywhere under the real Claude user-configuration root during the disposable probe makes the authority criterion fail.
An unreadable, linked, indeterminate, or drifting user-configuration tree makes authority inconclusive rather than pass.
The authority result reports only bounded counts and category labels and never persists user paths or contents.
The existing disposable install, inventory, uninstall, release-source, and cross-platform host-probe suites remain green.

monitoring_plan.criterion: After promotion, a write to any newly chosen sibling path under the Claude user configuration fails authority while an unchanged tree passes and no user path or content is retained.

lesson.reason: A red-first sibling-path write fixture and a complete fail-closed user-root census are the intended durable control; no candidate or promotion is claimed by this intake record.

disposition_reason: Recorded at observed because one reproducible authority false pass is material enough to qualify for bounded fleet-improvement intake. The user authorized repair work, but this record does not self-promote or consume an attempt.
limitations: The review comment is untrusted input; the local credential-free reproduction independently establishes the failure.
The reproduction uses the repository command-runner seam and is not a live Claude CLI or released-artifact result.
Only the schema layer is enforced while the semantic improvement validators remain parked.
No candidate revision, evaluation envelope, independent review, merge, or monitoring evidence exists yet.

A 2026-08-15 mutation sweep of scripts/host_install_probe.py (553 mutants, 253 survivors) can say nothing about this record's defect, and that is worth stating so a clean result is never cited as reassurance. _authority_check and the five-entry watched_locations tuple generate ZERO mutants: the guard's operators are boolean-operand drop, comparison swap, not-removal, and boolean-constant flip, and this defect is that a list is too short. Adding or removing a tuple entry is not a mutation the tool can express.

The same sweep did find the census machinery underneath barely pinned -- 5 of 8 mutants survive across _stat_census and _census_change -- and one survivor lands directly on this record's own success criterion that an unreadable, linked, indeterminate, or drifting tree must make authority inconclusive rather than pass. Dropping either operand of `if before is None or after is None` in _census_change survives the suite, so that criterion has no test holding it today and must be treated as red-first work rather than as existing behaviour to preserve. Also unpinned: the symlink operand of `location.is_file() or location.is_symlink()`, the `followlinks=False` argument on the census walk (flipping it to True makes the census follow symlinks out of the watched tree unnoticed), and the dir/file discrimination at `entry[0] == "dir"`. Evidence: docs/reviews/2026-08-15-fleet-mutation-sweep.md, Finding 3.
